summary: Full testing of new Organogram (org chart) feature. All 23 backend pytest cases PASS, all critical frontend flows verified end-to-end (Admin add/edit/delete, non-admin view-only, CMod-rank user gains edit, portal navigation). Feature is production-ready.
passed_tests: Backend: GET /api/organogram/can-edit returns true for Admin, false for SampleLMod, true for CModUser once they have a CMod node
Backend: GET /api/organogram/portal-users returns moderators with is_assigned flag
Backend: POST /api/organogram/nodes - validates rank in [CMod,MMod,SMod,LMod,Mod]; rejects duplicates; rejects invalid parent rank; rejects non-existent parent
Backend: PATCH /api/organogram/nodes/{id} - updates display_name, prevents cycles, prevents rank change that would invalidate child rank
Backend: DELETE /api/organogram/nodes/{id} - reparents children to deleted node's parent (verified)
Backend: 403 returned for non-admin/non-CMod on POST/PATCH/DELETE; GET allowed
Backend: 404 on delete of unknown node id
Backend: CMod-rank user (CModUser added as CMod) successfully creates new nodes
Frontend: /moderator/organogram loads after Admin login, shows CMOD/MMOD tier badges with SVG connector path between parent and child
Frontend: Admin sees Add Member button; dialog opens with portal user dropdown (filters out already-assigned users), rank select, parent select, display name input, profile picture upload
Frontend: Submitting form creates node and chart updates without full reload (saw 'Node added to organogram' toast and new card render)
Frontend: SampleLMod sees view-only mode - no Add/Edit/Delete buttons, 'View-only mode' message shown
Frontend: CModUser (organogram CMod) sees Add Member button + Edit/Delete on hover
Frontend: Moderator Portal 'Org Chart' quick-action button (portal-organogram-btn) navigates to /moderator/organogram
Frontend: Admin edit display name -> reflected in card immediately
Frontend: Admin delete node -> 'Removed from organogram' toast, card disappears, child reparented to grandparent (verified MMod->CMod after deletion)
action_items: Unrelated to organogram: A non-blocking 404 from /api/moderators/check-email-status appears on login page in console (pre-existing). Worth checking but did not affect any organogram flow.
critical_code_review_comments: organogram.py: serialize_node converts ISO strings back to datetime for response, but the OrgNode response_model accepts datetime. OK.
Cycle prevention in PATCH walks parent chain - correct.
Children reparent on delete uses node.parent_id (could be None) - correctly handled.
Profile picture base64 stored as-is with no size cap on backend (frontend caps 1.5MB). Consider also enforcing server-side limit to harden against direct API abuse.
Organogram.js (~530 lines) is approaching reasonable single-file size; further growth should be split.
All endpoints use _id projection exclusion correctly - no MongoDB ObjectId leak.
test_credentials: Admin/AdminTest123!, SampleLMod/Sample123!, CModUser/CModTest123! - all verified. Updated /app/memory/test_credentials.md with full set.
seed_data_creation: Tests create CModUser(CMod) -> SampleSMod(MMod) -> SampleMod1(Mod) hierarchy, then add SampleLMod(LMod) under MMod via CMod user. Final cleanup left an 'Updated Chief'/CModUser CMod node in the DB from the UI flow (no children). Main agent may wish to wipe organogram_nodes if a clean DB is desired.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Organogram feature is fully working. Backend regression tests are at /app/backend/tests/test_organogram.py (23 tests, 5.7s). All data-testids in spec are present and used. SVG connectors verified on screenshots. Permission model correctly checks Admin OR organogram CMod node.
